title: Drop dead UIBackgroundModes (fetch, remote-notification) from ios/Runner/Info.plist — no backing implementation exists
rule: Tier-2 config correctness / dead-target directive (no numbered coding-standards.md rule; general dead-code + AG posture)
why: Info.plist declares both `fetch` and `remote-notification` background modes, but AppDelegate.swift (6-18) implements no `application(_:performFetchWithCompletionHandler:)` or `application(_:didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler:)` override and never calls `registerForRemoteNotifications()`; pubspec.yaml has no `firebase_messaging` dependency; every reminder in NotificationGateway is scheduled locally via `zonedSchedule`. The keys were added wholesale in the initial iOS scaffold (b9d3a8b0) and never exercised. Concrete cost: Apple App Review Guideline 2.5.4 explicitly targets apps that declare background modes without a corresponding implementation (submission friction/rejection risk), and the stale declaration will mislead whoever next builds real push notifications into thinking server-side delivery already exists.
recommendation: Remove the `UIBackgroundModes` key (and its two entries) from Info.plist since notification delivery is 100% local today. If server push is genuinely planned, land the capability declaration in the same change as the `firebase_messaging` dependency, the AppDelegate handler(s), and `registerForRemoteNotifications()` — not ahead of the implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes key, or each remaining mode has a matching handler in AppDelegate.swift referenced by a Linear ticket.
grep -A2 'UIBackgroundModes' learning_tracker/ios/Runner/Info.plist returns nothing (or only modes with matching AppDelegate.swift handlers) — usable as a Rule-0 grep checker.

corrections: Lowered P2->P3: the stated 'concrete cost' (App Review rejection) is unlikely in practice for fetch+remote-notification specifically; only the maintenance/misleading-signal cost is solidly concrete, which fits P3 hygiene better than P2 design debt.
